title: 5 reasons why “I know what you did last summer” is better than “Scream”

commenti.body:
I'm a huge fan of the 90/00s teen film genre, I keep a separate area of my home dedicated to my collection.  Including both Scream and I Know What You Did Last Summer.  I first started watching Kevin Williamson stuff by way of Dawson's Creek by way of TBS, back in the mid aughts they used to run an annual summer vacation marathon where they'd show the series in order 2 episodes a day starting at 10am.  I still love the show, I'm actually in the midst of a rewatch right now.

That being said, I think I disagree with large parts of your analysis.

1. I feel like you're taking for granted how innovative the idea of a meta horror film was at the time.  I think you have some Seinfeld effect going on here because it had not been done before.  It was also one of the first, if not the first (and maybe only), major Hollywood slasher films to combine a legitimate whodunnit with the crazed serial killer.  Jason is Jason, Freddy is Freddy, most of the time the killer is either a known entity and the teens are fighting him OR the killer is an unknown entity and they don't understand what's happening.   In Scream, the whole thing becomes much more like a Hitchcock, where anyone could be the killer.

Also, while IKWYDLS is not nearly as meta as Scream, it's very much an homage to classic horror slashers.  Which does add a meta element and there is quite a bit of wink wink at the audience, it's just not quite as blatant as a character literally describing how to survive a slasher.

2. Drew Barrymore, Neve Campbell, Courtney Cox, Rose McGowan, all at the height of their careers and hotness.  I will give you that the male cast in IKWYDLS is hotter, but I've also always loved the casting of Skeet Ulrich because it was obviously done just because he has a passing resemblance to Johnny Depp (as a reference to Nightmare on Elm Street).

3. Come on man, the Scream soundtrack is legendary.  Nick Cave & the Bad Seeds "Red Right Hand" is so iconic in this film, plus that soft acoustic cover of "Don't Fear the Reaper", and the use of "Schools Out" by Alice Cooper when the school shuts down because of a murder is such a crazy take after the song had been used for decades as a celebration for the coming summer break. 

4. Don't get me wrong, I like the fisherman hook guy, and I think IKWYDLS is great, but Ghostface is definitely the more iconic of the two.  And I feel like it's made all the creepier by the fact that the mask was literally purchased at a real Halloween store.  It's just a normal mask that was already being mass produced and that, like in the film, any average person could have gone and got.  Which adds to the creepiness.

I personally liked Scream better, I thought it was a lot more inventive…and frankly a little scary. First horror flick I saw where cell phones were used as a plot device. 

The 90s slasher movies were pretty good and weren’t as campy as the 80s ones, which towards the end of the decade they got pretty bad. Hell, even Urban Legend had its moments.
Lol, Neve Cambell and Rose McGowan and the rest can’t hook Love Hewitts bra strap looks wise. Be honest.

Are you kidding me?  Rose McGowan x1000 over Jenifer Love Hewitt on her best day.  Especially if you're working in acting chops and what they had going for them at the time, you have Party of Five (where JLH was 2nd best to Neve Campbell already) vs Doom Generation.
Lmao! Nutty Rose? No way hose, not now not ever!

This is a terrible troll job. I pray for better times than this no effort shlock. Kudos for thinking people being hot is worth an entire paragraph for your argument though, takes a real intellect for that.
Wow — your argument is “no JLH is hotter”. Did you think you were in /r/movies?
